hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Unlike Part I, we must output all four Fridays of November 2023, even if no purchases were made on that day.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Generate all Fridays in November 2023 using a recursive CTE starting at '2023-11-03' and incrementing by 7 days.

hints.title: Query Construction
hints.text: Left join the generated Fridays table with Purchases on Friday = purchase_date and replace null sums with 0.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RECURSIVE Fridays AS (
    SELECT '2023-11-03' AS friday
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATE_ADD(friday, INTERVAL 7 DAY) 
    FROM Fridays
    WHERE friday < '2023-11-23'
) 
SELECT 
    WEEK(Fridays.friday, 1) - WEEK('2023-11-01', 1) + 1 AS week_of_month, 
    Fridays.friday AS purchase_date, 
    IFNULL(SUM(Purchases.amount_spend), 0) AS total_amount 
FROM Fridays 
LEFT JOIN Purchases ON (Fridays.friday = Purchases.purchase_date) 
GROUP BY Fridays.friday 
ORDER BY week_of_month;
```

variables: N: total records in Purchases table
complexity.notes: Recursive CTE calendar generation joined against sales records.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner joins omit Fridays that had zero purchases.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) extra space for 4 Friday date constants.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use recursive CTE or date series with left join to retain zero-purchase dates.

solutions.approach: Recursive CTE Calendar Generation and Left Join

solutions.approach: Recursive CTE Calendar Generation and Left Join
solutions.code:
WITH RECURSIVE Fridays AS (
    SELECT DATE '2023-11-03' AS friday
    UNION ALL
    SELECT (friday + INTERVAL '7 DAY')::DATE 
    FROM Fridays
    WHERE friday < DATE '2023-11-23'
) 
SELECT 
    (EXTRACT(WEEK FROM Fridays.friday) - EXTRACT(WEEK FROM DATE '2023-11-01') + 1)::INTEGER AS week_of_month, 
    Fridays.friday AS purchase_date, 
    COALESCE(SUM(Purchases.amount_spend), 0)::INTEGER AS total_amount 
FROM Fridays 
LEFT JOIN Purchases ON (Fridays.friday = Purchases.purchase_date) 
GROUP BY Fridays.friday 
ORDER BY week_of_month;

import pandas as pd

def friday_purchases_ii(purchases: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    fridays = pd.date_range(start='2023-11-01', end='2023-11-30', freq='W-FRI')
    f_df = pd.DataFrame({'friday': fridays})
    f_df['purchase_date'] = f_df['friday'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    start_week = pd.to_datetime('2023-11-01').isocalendar()[1]
    f_df['week_of_month'] = f_df['friday'].dt.isocalendar().week - start_week + 1
    
    p = purchases.copy()
    p['purchase_date'] = pd.to_datetime(p['purchase_date']).dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    p_grouped = p.groupby('purchase_date')['amount_spend'].sum().reset_index()
    
    merged = f_df.merge(p_grouped, on='purchase_date', how='left')
    merged['total_amount'] = merged['amount_spend'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return merged[['week_of_month', 'purchase_date', 'total_amount']].sort_values(by='week_of_month')
